h: Every Soul Shares in the Endless Ascent of Holiness

p: at the beginning of the passage that opens "Ish":
is the general principle of the Torah";
It appears from this whole matter
is the general principle of the entire Torah;
in the entire Torah and its mitzvos
is only to bring holiness into the heart,
"And you shall do all My mitzvos
"And you shall keep, etc., and do them;
I am Hashem Who sanctifies you"
put holiness into a person's heart,
as we say in their blessings,
"Who has sanctified us with His mitzvos and commanded us,"
and in the Kiddush of the day,
"Who has sanctified us with His mitzvos, etc.,"
and in prayer, "Sanctify us with Your mitzvos";
וְנֶאֱמַר עַל קַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה (שְׁמוֹת יט, ו)
and it says concerning the receiving of the Torah (Shemos 19:6):
"And you shall be, etc., and a holy nation";
"And you shall be holy people to Me";
"For you are a holy people, etc.";
And as for its saying "we have learned,"
it appears that it refers to the Baraisa
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כד, ה)
which is also in Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 24:5):
that it was said in a full assembly
because most of the main bodies of the Torah
is the essentials of the Torah.
And one may say, as I said,
that the intent is not the mitzvos in the parsha,
דְּזֶה אָמַר בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ
for that it states in Midrash Rabbah there afterward,
that the Ten Commandments are included in it;
rather it refers to its saying
one may say it is because there is much
that serves to bring in purity,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
as Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair said
and so it says in the Zohar here
is purified, and afterward is sanctified.")
And therefore it was said in a full assembly,
of which they said that had
even one of Yisrael been missing,
the Torah would not have been given;
for the six hundred thousand of the generation of the wilderness
are the six hundred thousand letters of the Torah;
for the root of each one's soul
or part of a letter of the Torah,
that letter would have been missing,
and a Sefer Torah that is missing
even the tip of a yud
in what it says, "You shall be holy,
"Just as I am holy, so too, etc."
meaning holy like Him, may He be blessed.
וְאַף שֶׁאָמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כד, ט)
And even though it says in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 24:9):
The verse says, 'For I am holy':
My holiness is above your holiness"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עַל פָּסוּק (דְּבָרִים יא, כב)
as they said on the pasuk (Devarim 11:22)
just as He is compassionate, etc.
But this is only according to one's grasp
of His attributes, may He be blessed;
and in truth His holiness, may He be blessed,
and likewise in a person's holiness
"The entire assembly, all of them are holy, etc.";
is not written in the Torah,
so certainly the truth was so.
But there is holiness above holiness:
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת אֱמוֹר (וַיִּקְרָא כא, ח)
as it is written in Parshas Emor (Vayikra 21:8):
he shall be holy to you,
for I, Hashem Who sanctifies you, am holy."
and He gives this as the reason
for the holiness of the Kohen relative to Yisrael:
for His holiness has no measure
and there are levels higher and higher
And we find that Rebbi is called in the Gemara
and in the Yerushalmi of Gittin (end of chapter 6)
"Just as the difference between the Holy of Holies
and the most profane of the profane,
so is the difference between me and Rabbi Yose."
Thus there are many levels in holiness.
And regarding the holiness of place
תְּנַן בְּפֶרֶק א דְּכֵלִים (כֵּלִים א, ו)
we learned in the first chapter of Keilim (Keilim 1:6)
that "there are ten levels of holiness";
and this is a division following the principle
that every holiness is divided into ten levels,
And presumably it is so also in the year:
and the four holinesses of the festivals,
which is a festival in its own right
is a level of holiness of its own;
and Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur:
each of which is a holiness of its own,
are each a holiness of its own;
and the revelation of Atika Kadisha,
and Rosh Chodesh is the end,
And so presumably in souls too
one should reckon ten levels of holiness:
Kohen Gadol, and the Kohen anointed for war,
Nasi, and Av Beis Din, and sage,
which counts eleven levels among the Kohanim;
and one may say that they are only ten,
for the anointed one and the one with additional garments
unless the anointed one has left office,
in which case he is an anointed one who has left office;
And the division of the levels
is according to one's grasp of His holiness, may He be blessed;
for His holiness too, may He be blessed,
For regarding the very essence of the Ein Sof
rather it is all from the side of the emanation of His holiness,
in that He emanated some perception
of His light, may He be blessed, to the created beings;
and so it goes on without measure,
And a person who sanctifies himself
but all is according to his grasp.
And when he reaches some level of holiness,
then there is revealed to him
the light of His holiness, may He be blessed,
that he has not yet reached;
and he goes back to sanctify himself
And when he reaches that level,
אָז הוּא מַשִּׂיג מַדְרֵגָה יוֹתֵר עֶלְיוֹנָה
then he perceives a yet higher level
of His holiness, may He be blessed;

p: And in Midrash Tanchuma (Kedoshim 2) it says:
'I am king and you are queen,' etc.
so too you shall be holy, etc."
it is a likeness to Him,
in the manner of a king and queen.
And this is as is known,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, the Torah
and just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is holy
and likewise in the souls of Yisrael;
for within the collective Knesses Yisrael
there is in each one a particular holiness.
And even in the sinners of Yisrael
for they are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate (Eruvin 19a),
and every mitzvah puts holiness in the heart.
it says in this parsha afterward,
גַּבֵּי מוֹלֶךְ וְאוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי (וַיִּקְרָא כ, ז)
"And you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy, etc.";
and it refers to separation from idolatry,
and it is from Toras Kohanim;
for the holiness of all the mitzvos
was already stated in "You shall be holy";
in a small measure of holiness;
and it took the most minimal case,
one who has no holiness at all
except that he separates from idolatry
and is not like all the nations
even this is enough to consider him
as one who comes to sanctify himself,
and he has already entered the holiness of Yisrael;
and through this, "and you shall be holy"
And it concludes, "For I am Hashem your God":
this is what they said in Yoma (39a),
that he is sanctified from Above,
for the World to Come, as is known.
But here it does not say
as it is written at the beginning of the parsha;
for in so slight a holiness as this,
to His holiness, may He be blessed, at all.
And at the end of Parshas Shemini (Vayikra 11:44–45),
in the warning against creeping creatures,
"And you shall sanctify yourselves, etc., for I am holy;
and do not, etc., with any creeping thing, etc.;
and you shall be holy, for I am holy."
מִזֶּה דָּרְשׁוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (נג, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
from this they expounded in Berachos (53b, at the end);
on the strength of the expression "Hashem your God";
and it is surprising that he did not notice
is absent there in Parshas Kedoshim,
so one would perforce have to emend
the wording of the Gemara there.
Rather one should emend as the Gra there,
that they refer to the pasuk in Shemini,
of which they said in Bava Metzia (61b)
דְּעַל כֵּן אָמַר שָׁם הַמַּעֲלֶה כוּ׳
that it therefore says there "Who brings up, etc.,"
from these, which are loathsome, it is enough;
and so too the first and last waters
and the oil of Berachos there
And the Ramban, at the beginning of Parshas Kedoshim,
for the positive commandment of "be holy,"
and the Gur Aryeh there wonders,
But he should rather have asked
how could they attach oil to a pasuk,
and nowadays is not practiced at all?
that in this mitzvah there is no
only that each person sanctify himself
in what is permitted to him,
and whatever separation a person practices
And the Sages established them as a mitzvah and an obligation;
one who does this and the like,
the grime and the loathsomeness and the like,
of "You shall be holy," of "You shall sanctify yourselves";
this particular is not an obligation
for the Torah did not intend
but rather each one should see
and to keep away from loathsomeness and grime
that seems to him fit to keep away from,
אַף שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שׁוּם סְפֵק אִיסּוּר
even though it involves no doubt of a prohibition at all,
only so as to be in cleanliness;
וְעַיֵּין רַשִׁ״י עֵירוּבִין (נג, סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
and see Rashi, Eruvin 53a, at the end.
Until here from his holy manuscript.
